scope: Offline first-release learning content. Guidance is not remote diagnosis or printer authorization.

articles.title: Start your first print safely
articles.summary: Bring in a model, prepare it on a real plate, then inspect the toolpath. Alloy keeps physical printing locked until the exact job and printer are qualified.
articles.scope: Applies to every printer. It does not confirm a clean plate, loaded filament, or a safe room.
steps: Choose Explore if you want to learn before pairing a printer.
Confirm the printer, nozzle, plate and feed route before choosing material.
Stay nearby to watch the first layer; estimates are planning aids, not guarantees.

articles.title: Bring in a model
articles.summary: Import an STL, OBJ, 3MF or supported STEP source from your phone. A successful import means Alloy can display the geometry; it does not yet mean it is printable.
articles.scope: Inspect warnings and dimensions before relying on an imported model.
steps: Use Library or Import model.
Confirm the model name and bounds.
Keep the original source file available for revision.

articles.title: Place it on a plate
articles.summary: Arrange the real model geometry within the selected printer’s printable area. Move, rotate and scale deliberately, then inspect the plate.
articles.scope: A visible fit cannot prove physical clearance, adhesion or print success.
steps: Select the intended plate.
Keep every object inside the printable area.
Re-check after changing scale or orientation.

articles.title: Match a recipe to reality
articles.summary: A recipe only makes sense when printer, nozzle, plate, material and feed route all describe the physical setup in front of you.
articles.scope: An imported or bundled profile is not direct-send approval.
steps: Read the selected printer and material labels.
Compare them to the real setup.
Re-slice after changing a recipe.

articles.title: Inspect before export
articles.summary: Review layer one, bridges, thin features, warnings, estimates and any generated supports before sharing or exporting an artifact.
articles.scope: Inspection finds obvious issues; it is not a guarantee of a successful physical job.
steps: Check layer one first.
Review warnings and unknown estimates.
Use the physical printer as the source of truth during a print.

articles.title: Choose material and feed route
articles.summary: The same material name can still be unsafe or unsuitable when the spool, storage, route, plate or nozzle does not match.
articles.scope: Bambu-published material capability is separate from Alloy direct-send qualification.
articles.source: Alloy A1 mini material contract v1
steps: Start with the exact printer’s material record.
Confirm the feed route.
Treat an unknown or tangled spool as not ready.

articles.title: Know when to stop
articles.summary: Smoke, smell, collisions, loose cables, leaking material and uncertain machine state need supervision, not a setting change.
articles.scope: This app does not provide electrical or hotend repair instructions.
steps: Stop and supervise if it is safe.
Do not touch hot or moving parts.
Use current manufacturer support guidance.

articles.title: The first layer
articles.summary: The first layer is the foundation of the print. A clean, even line that stays attached is a good sign—not a guarantee for the rest of the job.
articles.scope: Visual teaching aid only; it cannot diagnose your plate, nozzle or filament.
articles.source: Alloy original illustration · learning contract v1
steps: Before starting, confirm the selected plate and material match the physical setup.
Watch the first layer without touching hot or moving parts.
If lines lift, bunch up, or the nozzle collides, stop and use the symptom guide.

articles.title: Material, spool and feed route
articles.summary: Material is not the whole setup. Filament diameter, spool condition, feed route, nozzle, plate and profile must agree.
articles.scope: Compatibility labels describe Bambu-published capability. They do not qualify an Alloy direct-send job.
articles.source: Bambu Lab product/filament guidance reviewed in Alloy audit · 2026-09-28
steps: Start with the material record for your selected printer, not a generic material name.
For A1 mini, begin with 1.75 mm filament on the external holder/direct path unless the selected route says otherwise.
Unknown, damp, tangled, near-empty, or route-incompatible spools are not direct-send ready.

articles.title: Layers, walls, infill and G-code
articles.summary: A slicer turns a model into layers and motion. Walls shape the outside; infill supports the inside; G-code/toolpaths tell a machine how to move.
articles.scope: Toolpath review can reveal obvious issues but cannot prove a successful physical print.
steps: Inspect layer 1 first, then bridges, thin features and highlighted warnings.
Use supports and brims only when the selected profile can represent them; Alloy support output is not direct-send qualified.
Export can be available even when direct print remains locked.

articles.title: Model and build plate
articles.summary: A model is the shape; the build plate is where its first layer begins.
articles.scope: A visible model is not proof it fits the selected printer.
steps: Check the model size.
Keep every part inside the highlighted printable area.
Use Undo after moving or arranging a part.

articles.title: Nozzle
articles.summary: The nozzle is the heated tip that places filament. Its size changes what a recipe can safely plan.
articles.scope: Do not touch a nozzle or plate while hot or moving.
steps: Confirm the selected nozzle size.
Use a matching profile.
Let the printer cool before any physical inspection.

articles.title: Profile
articles.summary: A profile is a documented agreement between printer, nozzle, plate, material and quality settings.
articles.scope: An imported or selected profile is not an Alloy print qualification.
steps: Match the profile to the real setup.
Review amber items.
Re-slice after changing a recipe.

articles.title: Walls
articles.summary: Walls are the solid outer shells of a print. They are different from the pattern inside.
articles.scope: Strength depends on shape, material and orientation as well as walls.
steps: Change wall count only in Recipe.
Re-slice.
Compare the revised estimate.

articles.title: Infill
articles.summary: Infill is the pattern inside a part. More is not automatically better or stronger.
articles.scope: Estimate changes are planning values, not measurements.
steps: Choose a documented recipe.
Compare time and material estimates.
Inspect thin walls separately.

articles.title: Orientation
articles.summary: Which side faces the plate can change strength direction, finish and support need.
articles.scope: A suggested orientation needs user review; Alloy does not guarantee success.
steps: Try the suggested orientation.
Review the plate and overhangs.
Re-slice after accepting it.

articles.title: Brim
articles.summary: A brim is extra first-layer material around a part that can help it remain attached.
articles.scope: Use only when the selected profile represents it and remove it after cooling.
steps: Preview the brim.
Review material use.
Wait for cooling before removal.

articles.title: Supports
articles.summary: Supports are temporary scaffolding below difficult areas. They use material and can affect surface finish.
articles.scope: Alloy support output is not direct-send qualified until its separate parity gate passes.
steps: Review the overhang.
Treat the support warning as a blocker for direct send.
Inspect the preview before export.

articles.title: Estimates and cleanup
articles.summary: Model material, supports, purge, priming and waste are different quantities. Unknown values stay unknown.
articles.scope: Remaining spool is an estimate unless fresh telemetry or a user measurement says otherwise.
steps: Read each estimate label.
Keep a material reserve.
Do not treat an estimate as a guarantee.

articles.title: Nothing sticks to the plate
articles.summary: Symptom: early lines lift, drag, or gather at the nozzle. Likely causes include plate condition, setup mismatch, or filament condition; Alloy cannot identify which one remotely.
articles.scope: Use only reversible observations. Do not touch the nozzle, plate, or moving axes while hot or active.
articles.source: Alloy troubleshooting contract v1 · official support escalation required for persistent faults
steps: If the nozzle is colliding or the print is loose near moving parts, cancel only if it is safe to reach the printer.
After the machine is cool and idle, compare the physical plate, material and selected profile; do not silently continue with a mismatch.
Save the job details and use current Bambu support guidance if the symptom continues.

articles.title: Stringing, blobs or rough surfaces
articles.summary: Symptom: fine threads, blobs or uneven surfaces. Material condition and recipe choices can contribute, but a symptom is not a remote diagnosis.
articles.scope: Do not change temperatures or machine hardware based on a generic card. Use a reviewed recipe and manufacturer guidance.
articles.source: Alloy troubleshooting contract v1 · official material guidance
steps: Record the selected material, nozzle, plate, profile and visible symptom.
Check the spool for the state you can safely observe: label, feed route, tangles and moisture/storage history.
Use the filament maker’s current recommendations or Bambu support for persistent results.

articles.title: Stop and supervise the printer
articles.summary: Smoke, burning smell, grinding/collision, loose wires, damaged cables, a leaking hotend, or a loose print near moving parts need immediate human attention—not an app tutorial.
articles.scope: Do not dismantle hot parts, work on mains power, force moving axes, bypass protection, or update firmware from this guide.
articles.source: Alloy safety boundary · follow current manufacturer safety/support guidance
steps: Stop and supervise the printer; use its normal cancel/emergency procedure only if it is safe to reach.
Do not continue through troubleshooting while heat, power or moving hardware is unsafe.
Save non-secret job details, then use current manufacturer support or qualified service.

articles.title: Printer state is not confirmed
articles.summary: A network request is not proof that a printer received or acted on it. Stale or missing telemetry means Alloy must not claim a job is running.
articles.scope: Alloy never bypasses certificate, recovery, native-engine, profile or physical-printer gates.
articles.source: Alloy transport safety contract v1 · reviewed 2026-09-28
steps: Treat the printer’s physical panel and current official app as the source of truth when telemetry is stale.
Do not retry by removing certificate or readiness safeguards.
Review the saved job record and reconnect only through the normal pairing path.

articles.title: Corners lift or the part warps
articles.summary: Symptom: edges lift from the plate. Plate condition, geometry, material and ambient conditions can contribute.
articles.scope: Do not add an enclosure or change heat settings from generic advice.
steps: If a loose part risks contact, stop and supervise.
Review plate, material and profile identity after cooling.
Use current manufacturer guidance for a controlled retry.

articles.title: Gaps or weak-looking lines
articles.summary: Symptom: missing lines or gaps. Feed resistance, material condition and nozzle state are possible causes.
articles.scope: Do not pull filament through a powered feeder or open a hot assembly.
steps: Stop if grinding or a collision is present.
Record material and feed-route details.
Use current printer and filament guidance.

articles.title: Layers are misaligned
articles.summary: Symptom: upper layers move sideways. An obstruction or collision needs a stop-and-check path.
articles.scope: Never force axes by hand or continue an uncertain collision.
steps: Stop and supervise if the printer is active.
Do not force moving hardware.
Save evidence and use official support guidance.

articles.title: Detached print or spaghetti
articles.summary: Symptom: printed material is no longer attached and may enter the moving toolhead area.
articles.scope: A detached print needs human supervision; the app cannot assess the physical hazard remotely.
steps: Cancel only if normal controls are safe to reach.
Do not touch hot or moving parts.
Save a photo and review the first layer.

articles.title: Spool, tangle or feed-route problem
articles.summary: Symptom: filament does not move as expected. A spool label alone cannot prove compatibility or condition.
articles.scope: TPU and AMS-lite compatibility must come from the exact material record.
articles.source: Alloy A1 mini material contract v1
steps: Confirm the selected material and route.
Inspect only when the printer is cool and idle.
Use manufacturer guidance for persistent feed issues.

articles.title: Temperature warning or unexpected heat
articles.summary: A temperature label is profile data, not proof that the machine is safe to touch.
articles.scope: Burning smell, smoke, damaged wiring or leaking material requires manufacturer support or qualified service.
steps: Stop and supervise if it is safe.
Do not dismantle hot or electrical parts.
Use current manufacturer safety guidance.

articles.title: Loose wire or damaged cable
articles.summary: Do not treat damaged wiring as a tuning problem.
articles.scope: No in-app repair procedure is provided for electrical parts.
steps: Stop using the printer if safe.
Do not bypass protection.
Contact current manufacturer support or qualified service.

articles.title: Leaking hotend or molten material
articles.summary: Molten material outside its normal path can damage hardware and needs a safe stop path.
articles.scope: Do not pull, scrape or dismantle hot components.
steps: Stop and supervise if safe.
Keep clear of hot moving parts.
Use manufacturer service guidance.

articles.title: An interrupted job needs review
articles.summary: An unknown upload or interrupted print must not be retried automatically.
articles.scope: Alloy recovery locks remain in effect until fresh state is reviewed.
steps: Check the physical printer state.
Review the saved job record.
Reconnect only through the normal path.

articles.title: Unknown or incompatible material
articles.summary: A material name without a matching route and profile is not direct-send ready.
articles.scope: A1 mini not-recommended classes remain blocked from direct send.
articles.source: Alloy A1 mini material contract v1
steps: Do not prepare a direct job.
Choose a documented compatible material.
Keep the job as inspect/export only until qualified.

articles.title: First-layer lines have gaps
articles.summary: Symptom: the first layer has separated lines or uncovered patches. Treat it as a setup review, not proof of one cause.
articles.scope: Do not reach into the printer or tune hardware while it is active.
steps: Watch from a safe distance and stop if the part drags or collides.
After cooling, compare the selected plate, nozzle, material and recipe with the real setup.
Keep the result as evidence and use current manufacturer guidance for a controlled retry.

articles.title: First-layer material bunches at the nozzle
articles.summary: Symptom: material gathers or follows the nozzle instead of forming an even line. A loose moving print needs supervision.
articles.scope: Do not remove material near a hot nozzle or moving axes.
steps: Cancel only through normal controls if it is safe to reach them.
Let the printer cool before any approved plate or material observation.
Review the first-layer preview and official support guidance before retrying.

articles.title: Bridges sag or droop
articles.summary: Symptom: material spanning an open gap hangs below the intended shape. Geometry, material and recipe can all contribute.
articles.scope: Do not treat an export preview as a strength guarantee.
steps: Inspect the bridge and layer preview before changing the model.
Record the selected material and profile.
Use a reviewed orientation or manufacturer recipe guidance for the next attempt.

articles.title: A seam or scar appears on the surface
articles.summary: Symptom: a visible vertical line or small surface mark appears where a layer begins or ends. It is a finish question, not a safety diagnosis.
articles.scope: Do not change unknown machine settings while a print is running.
steps: Compare the visible mark with the layer preview.
Record orientation and surface choice.
Adjust only a reviewed recipe and re-slice for a later attempt.

articles.title: Unexpected grinding or noisy motion
articles.summary: Symptom: movement sounds rough, blocked or different from normal. Noise plus a collision risk needs an immediate stop path.
articles.scope: Never force axes, belts or the toolhead by hand.
steps: Stop and supervise if it is safe.
Do not force moving hardware or continue a suspected collision.
Save non-secret details and use current manufacturer service guidance.

articles.title: The model does not fit the printable area
articles.summary: Symptom: a model or part extends beyond the selected plate boundary. A smaller machine profile cannot be solved by ignoring the boundary.
articles.scope: The displayed profile must match the physical printer and plate.
articles.source: Alloy geometry safety contract v1 · reviewed 2026-09-29
steps: Confirm the selected printer profile and plate.
Move, split or scale the model deliberately.
Re-check every part boundary before slicing.

articles.title: The spool is nearly empty or material ran out
articles.summary: Symptom: the available spool amount is uncertain or the printer reports a runout. A remaining-material estimate is not a measurement.
articles.scope: Do not assume a substitution spool has the same recipe or feed-route compatibility.
articles.source: Alloy material safety contract v1 · reviewed 2026-09-29
steps: Treat the physical spool and printer state as the source of truth.
Confirm material, route and profile before any replacement.
Keep direct send unavailable when the resulting job state is uncertain.

articles.title: The spool may be damp or poorly stored
articles.summary: Symptom: a material history suggests moisture or storage uncertainty. Alloy cannot determine moisture from a name or a picture.
articles.scope: Use the material maker's current drying and storage guidance; do not improvise hot handling.
articles.source: Alloy material safety contract v1 · reviewed 2026-09-29
steps: Record the material and storage history you know.
Review the exact manufacturer's guidance.
Keep the setup as inspect/export only if its condition is unknown.

articles.title: The plate has residue or an uncertain surface
articles.summary: Symptom: the build surface looks marked, oily or unknown. A plate label alone does not prove it is ready for the selected recipe.
articles.scope: Use only current printer-maker cleaning guidance after the printer is cool and idle.
articles.source: Alloy first-layer safety contract v1 · reviewed 2026-09-29
steps: Wait until the machine is cool and idle.
Compare the physical plate with the selected plate label.
Follow current manufacturer-approved preparation guidance.

articles.title: An exported job is rejected
articles.summary: Symptom: a receiving app or tool does not accept an exported artifact. Generic sharing is not Bambu Handy compatibility evidence.
articles.scope: Do not rename, modify or force an unknown printer package into a send flow.
steps: Keep the original artifact and its hash.
Review package validation and recipient requirements.
Do not claim recipient acceptance until it is independently verified.

articles.title: The printer is busy or state is unclear
articles.summary: Symptom: the printer reports a current job, preparation state or stale status. The app must not start a second job from a local assumption.
articles.scope: Fresh authenticated telemetry is required before any future send path can proceed.
articles.source: Alloy transport safety contract v1 · reviewed 2026-09-29
steps: Check the printer's physical panel first.
Wait for fresh state through the normal pairing path.
Do not retry a start request while state is unconfirmed.

articles.title: Alloy closed during a slice or job
articles.summary: Symptom: the app was interrupted while preparing or observing a job. A restart must surface recovery review, never silently continue.
articles.scope: Recovery is review-only until fresh state and artifact identity are available.
articles.source: Alloy recovery safety contract v1 · reviewed 2026-09-29
steps: Reopen Alloy and read the recovery record.
Check the physical printer state before any further action.
Do not accept automatic retry or resume for an unknown transaction.

articles.title: Can I print it just because it imported?
articles.summary: No. Import confirms Alloy could read enough geometry to display the model; it does not establish that the model is manifold, correctly scaled, within the selected printer’s envelope, or safe to print.
articles.scope: Treat import, slicing, export and physical-print approval as separate stages.
steps: Review dimensions and mesh warnings.
Choose the exact printer and plate before arranging.
Inspect the slice and any warnings before export.

articles.title: What is the difference between STL and 3MF?
articles.summary: STL generally carries surface geometry. 3MF can carry richer project information such as multiple objects or settings, depending on how it was authored. Neither extension proves that its contents or embedded settings are correct.
articles.scope: Imported project data may be incomplete or incompatible; the selected Alloy setup remains the source for planning.
steps: Confirm the object count and dimensions after import.
Review 3MF plates and settings instead of assuming they transferred correctly.
Keep the original file for revisions.

articles.title: What does slicing do?
articles.summary: A slicer converts the arranged model and selected recipe into layer-by-layer toolpaths. Preview helps you inspect those paths; it cannot predict every machine, material or environment failure.
articles.scope: Native engine and profile parity are still being qualified; a generated preview is not a print guarantee.
steps: Check the first layer and later layers in preview.
Review supports, thin features, warnings and estimates.
Do not send a job while its qualification gate is closed.

articles.title: How accurate are time and filament estimates?
articles.summary: Treat them as planning estimates. Real use can differ because of purge and cleaning, supports, calibration, motion limits, temperature behavior and the actual profile. Unknown values should remain unknown, not be presented as measured facts.
articles.scope: Do not use estimates alone to decide that a spool or printer is ready.
steps: Check whether supports and purge are included in the reported value.
Leave margin for waste and failed starts.
Compare estimates with observed results only after a supervised print.

articles.title: When should I use supports?
articles.summary: Supports hold up geometry that cannot be printed reliably over open space. They consume material and time and may affect surface quality; tree and standard supports behave differently.
articles.scope: Support generation and Bambu-specific parity are not yet qualified for physical production use.
steps: Inspect unsupported overhangs in the preview.
Compare supported and support-free orientations.
Keep generated supports review-only until the support gate passes.

articles.title: How do I choose between A1 mini, A1 and P1S?
articles.summary: Choose the model that is physically in front of you, then confirm its plate, nozzle and feed route. A1 mini has the smaller build area; never select another printer just to make an oversized object appear to fit.
articles.scope: A loaded profile is not proof of the printer’s firmware, configuration or physical condition.
articles.source: Alloy initial Bambu profile contract v1
steps: Read the printer label in the app and compare it with the machine.
Check the selected plate and build-envelope warnings.
If the model does not fit, scale or split it only when that change is intended.

articles.title: Which spool and material should I use?
articles.summary: Use the printer’s Materials & compatibility guide to review Bambu-listed material capability, spool form and feed-route notes. A material being listed does not prove that a particular spool fits, is dry, or is qualified for Alloy direct-send.
articles.scope: A1 mini material/spool records are planning guidance; unknown fit or feed routes must stay blocked.
steps: Identify the exact material and spool form.
Confirm the feed route and any drying requirement.
Do not force a spool or route that is not listed for the selected setup.

articles.title: Can Alloy send this directly or open it in Bambu Handy?
articles.summary: Not yet as a validated production handoff. Alloy’s direct-send path remains fail-closed while native slicing, job packaging and printer acceptance are being qualified. An export or share action must not be mistaken for Bambu Handy acceptance.
articles.scope: Direct-send, validated Bambu-ready export and Bambu Handy import require separate completed evidence gates.
steps: Use only the currently available review/export actions.
Check the current release gate status before relying on an output file.
Do not bypass the send lock or treat a generic 3MF as a validated printer job.

articles.title: What should I do if the printer behaves unexpectedly?
articles.summary: Stop and supervise if it is safe to do so. Smoke, unusual odor, collisions, damaged cables, leaking material, or unknown motion state are not problems to solve by blindly changing slicer settings.
articles.scope: Alloy learning content is not a remote diagnosis or a repair guide for hot, moving or electrical parts.
steps: Use the printer’s physical controls if safe.
Keep clear of hot and moving parts.
Follow current manufacturer support guidance.
